title: How to Win My Heart
essence: The poet walks down from the white temple to a corner café on the harbor of the heavens and sits at a small table, watching couples, while the tide comes in under the boats. Dusk counts out Jupiter's moons over the water; his younger self watches from the rail, the elders pray with their pearls, and his love letters burn on the quay stones. He harvests a field of scarlet poppies and purple blossoms until it flowers out of his own arms, and then, across the water, a distant window comes into focus with a woman in it, and he takes off his sunglasses and says hello.
palette_notes: Bay blue #465fb1 is the poem's colour in film/poems.json and the dusk sky over the harbor; harbor teal #0f5f63 and night navy #10243f are the water under the boardwalk and the night pier (932cb5b5_2, 3238a164_1, fc83bfee_0). Lantern gold #f0a64a is the café's string lights and paper lanterns (22ddf809_2, 932cb5b5_2). Quay grey #5c6670 is wet stone. The two flower colours are the accents: scarlet poppy #c8231e and purple blossom #7a3fa0, and SHE's red dress takes the poppy scarlet so the field and the window rhyme. Linen cream #e9dcc4 is the couples' summer clothes and the letters.

full_text.line: I want you to notice me in a corner cafe
at the Harbor of the Heavens, wandering in thought,
discovering water on Jupiter's moons,
healing the sick with silent prayers
and molding a better world to return to
with every pulsing beat after walking alone.
I want you to really notice me
with the distances we couldn't avoid
and our younger selves watching and dreaming,
while our elders clutch their pearls,
hold their faith and breath closely,
freeing their worries peacefully.
I've journeyed beyond any place you can conceivably be.
So I thought, life has burned all of my love stories.
All ends led to losses,
victory-less seasons for a man that wanted just one win.
I could celebrate forever.
Ice has frozen and thawed
friendships in death and departure.
I've learned to love myself more,
manage loss and harvest a wizardry more brilliant
than the scarlet poppies and purple blossoms
that time and tears have disclaimed.
Yet from a distant window, beautiful and calm,
hope tells me you'll see me.
And if you notice me and capture my eyes
as you refocus yours,
stepping back and letting them say hello,
all the fatigue of wandering alone in thought,
in winless seasons and scarlet poppies
won't prevent me from sharing a smile
worth the promise of my heart.

insights: One quantity per movement and it only goes one way: tide in, dark down, smoke up, field down, focus in. Pick the object that shows each number and never let it turn round.
Build the harbor as one tonal pass (sky, mud, water, quay) so day, dusk and night are the same set relit, and the tide is a moving line, not a redrawn object.
SHE is tiny and far: give her a dedicated small-scale head and keep her eyes to seven points; at full puppet scale she will read as a doll.
The becoming must stay HIS body with flowers growing out of it; a torso-and-stems substitute reads as a scarecrow.
The red of her dress is the poppy red: the field he harvests and the woman he hopes for are the same colour.

Transcript corrections from the treatment: 'Ice has frozen in thought' is 'Ice has frozen and thawed friendships'; 'at time and tears have just claimed' is 'that time and tears have disclaimed'; 'windless seasons' is 'winless seasons'.

Atlas: the halfworld frames (foundry/13-02, 13-03) already solve the poem in flat halftone cut-out: boats, chapel crosses, a gable window, couples as single silhouettes. Use them as the style key for every distance layer.

Atlas: the pier café hero (striped awning, plank deck, masts, bulb string) is a single reusable build; plan it so the window wall can carry a reflection layer for the YOUNG_POET beat and the 13.5 reverse.
Atlas: frame the reflection first and let the subject arrive into it; the bay's whole camera language is low over water.
Atlas: the haze rise at 13.6 is the same build as 14.0; build it once in 13.
future: The harbor, the temple on its rise and the boats are what the haze takes first in 14.
The poppy field is the 'field' card in 14's reel.
The couples-in-orbit move becomes 14's two entwined muses (the same turn, both him).
The window motif closes here as a window that looks back; in 14 the window stays shut and he chooses a door.

atlas.district_language: Mirror Thread Bay is water first: reflection before subject. Every set card that touches the water gets a doubled, rippled copy beneath it, and we often frame the reflection and let the person arrive into it. Daytime here is turquoise and calm (13.0-13.5), then the haze rises off the water (13.6). Paint the quay as old harbour stone with the flood line at +4 m everywhere, tide boards at every pier (white boards with black height marks), benches facing the water. The café is teal paint with whitewash trim, plank deck, slate roof, striped awnings, string lights, ships' masts behind. Light technology is daylight on water: one big coded caustic shimmer on the underside of awnings and the café ceiling. Code the shimmer; paint the stone. The one other light is the haze, an orange-to-white wash that rises from the bottom of frame at the end. Never show neon or the spire city in close here; the Atlantis skyline is a far flat silhouette band across the water only.

staging.name: Walk from the temple around the harbor
staging.shot: Long-lens lateral: camera tracks right along the promenade, the water and two moored boats between camera and the poet (boats and rail as front layer, him mid, quay buildings and the temple's white rise far back). He walks right to left past the drowned atrium's glowing window. Reflections lead: the shot opens on his reflection in the water strip.

staging.name: The corner cafe table
staging.shot: Static medium: the poet at the corner table by the window, espresso cup, sunglasses on; foreground two out-of-focus couple silhouettes at a near table; the window behind shows the bay. Eyeline cuts to the other tables: couples leaning in, orbiting.

staging.name: Distances, younger selves, praying elders
staging.shot: The café window glass as a semi-transparent card: his face reflected with YOUNG_POET's small face appearing beside it on the outside of the glass. Cut to two silhouettes on opposite shores (flat halftone layers). Cut to a quiet wide of a church: rows of dark pews, one lancet window, two elders with pearls and a rosary in the second pew.

staging.name: Victory-less seasons (inner montage)
staging.shot: Slow push in on his still face at the table, then match cuts: a lone traveller on a far road, the love letters burning on the quay stones at night, a dusty trophy case, flowers frozen in an ice block. Each insert is a single plate with one moving element.

staging.name: Harvesting the poppies
staging.shot: High top-down over the field: rows of scarlet poppy and purple spike cards in strips, the cut half as stubble; he moves along a row cutting. Close-up: the armful against his chest, light flowing from the flowers into him, then the same flowers growing out of his hands.

staging.name: From a distant window
staging.shot: Reverse from outside, across the water: the café window as a lit frame in the teal wall, him inside. Rack focus (coded blur swap between layers) from his reflection to his eyes. Then his POV across the bay: a far gable with one lit window, a woman in red in it, which sharpens from a soft card to a crisp one. He takes off the sunglasses.

staging.name: Stands and walks the harbor
staging.shot: Follow from behind along the waterline, the rail as a front strip; the frame widens (pull the layers apart) as the haze rises off the water from the bottom of frame, orange then white, erasing the far shore first, then the boats, then the quay.
